holidays.name: National Pickle Day
holidays.description: A salute to everything brined, briny and crunchy. Dill spears, bread-and-butter chips, sour gherkins and even pickled everything else are all invited. Crack open a jar, build a pickle plate, or just eat one straight from the jar.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance. Its exact origin is unclear, but it has become a fixture on the November food-holiday calendar.
holidays.funFact: Every pickle starts out as a cucumber. The brine and time do the rest, and the cucumber has been preserved this way for thousands of years.

holidays.name: National Spicy Guacamole Day
holidays.description: A day to give your guacamole a kick. Add jalapeños, serranos, a dash of hot sauce or a pinch of cayenne to the mashed avocado, then grab a bag of chips.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin, celebrated by avocado and chile fans alike.
holidays.funFact: The word guacamole comes from the Aztec Nahuatl word ahuacamolli, which roughly means avocado sauce.

holidays.name: National Cacio e Pepe Day
holidays.description: A tribute to the Roman pasta dish made from only a few ingredients: pasta, Pecorino Romano cheese and black pepper. It sounds simple, but getting the sauce silky instead of clumpy is a famous kitchen challenge.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It celebrates a classic dish of Roman cuisine.
holidays.funFact: The name means cheese and pepper in Italian. The dish is often linked to shepherds, who could carry the dry, long-lasting ingredients with them.
